Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-22
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees (recorded): Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Karen Meyers (Lacerta CISO), Dr. Alan Ruiz (Head of ML), Sofia Lopez (Cloud Eng)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 45ish minutes on the calendar. Quick round of intros?
[00:08] Karen (CISO): Thanks Jordan, hi I'm Karen Meyers I'm CISO at Lacerta. My team is looking at inference hosting for a new clinical-assist product, lots of PHI concerns so we'll ask the usual thing.
[00:18] Jordan (AE): Absolutely. Priya, want to intro yourself?
[00:20] Priya (SE): Yeah hi I'm Priya, I'm one of the solutions engineers who helps map security and infra requirements to our Dedicated and Private deployments and run any initial benchmarks.
[00:28] Dr. Alan (Head of ML): Alan here, lead for the ML stack, curious about latency and whether we can keep kv cache warm in a private setup.
[00:36] Sofia (Cloud Eng): Sofia, I'm on the infra side, cluster configs, network, and Okta SSO stuff.
[00:40] Jordan (AE): Great — quick agenda: cover compliance posture (SOC2/ISO), identity (SSO/Sam-el), RBAC, audit logs and retention, KMS and key management, and then deployment options and next steps. Sound good?
[00:50] Karen (CISO): Yes, let's jump into SOC2. We need to know if you're SOC 2 Type II and how often audits run and what in-scope controls are for inference/data processing. Also any recent exceptions.
[01:05] Jordan (AE): We're SOC2 Type II for the platform layer; we run annual audits and the scope covers our control plane and hosted inference service. Priya, do you want to add specifics on the report and where we draw the line for Private deployments?
[01:18] Priya (SE): Sure. The SOC2 report we can share is the most recent 2026 Type II, it shows control coverage for access controls, change management, incident response. For Private/VPC deployments the control plane still sits with Redwood in a customer-dedicated control plane unless you opt for the on‑prem package — that on‑prem option can be added for fully air-gapped needs. Note: some wording in the report refers to "model hosting" generically, we're happy to annotate which services are in-scope for your deployment.
[01:43] Karen (CISO): Cool. Do you have ISO 27001?
[01:46] Jordan (AE): Not at the platform level yet — ISO is roadmaped, we have some customers that require it and we've started gap remediation. We can share our ISO gap assessment.
[01:56] Karen (CISO): Ok please send the gap assessment. Also we need to map where PHI flows — in Hosted we assume tokens and prompts transit Redwood infra; what about encryption at rest and in transit?
[02:10] Priya (SE): All in-transit is TLS 1.2/1.3. At rest we encrypt datastore and logs; we support customer-managed keys via KMS for Dedicated and Private — for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with our KMS, but you can bring your own KMS for Dedicated and Private with HSM support if needed. Occasionally the transcript generator hears that as K-M-S or "KMS" spelled out, so apologies if audio is weird.
[02:36] Dr. Alan (Head of ML): For inference speed, how does customer KMS affect latency? We don't want extra round trips per token.
[02:45] Priya (SE): Good Q. KMS operations are used for key wrapping/unwrapping at session startup, not per token. We maintain an in-memory wrapping key and use KMIP/HSM-backed keys for rewraps periodically. There shouldn't be per-token KMS calls. We do prefetch and keep key material in-memory for sessions.
[03:05] Sofia (Cloud Eng): Can you support our Okta SSO? We use SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning and role mappings.
[03:12] Jordan (AE): Yes, we integrate with Okta — SAML 2.0 SSO + SCIM for user provisioning and group sync. Our RBAC supports role templates and custom roles; Priya can show the mapping doc.
[03:24] Priya (SE): To add detail: you can map Okta groups to Redwood roles (admin, platform-engineer, app-integrator, read-only). We also support just-in-time provisioning and can restrict API access with token-scoped roles. There's sometimes slight differences in the SAML assertions fields — we've seen the Sam-el assertion mislabel in older logs — but we can work through the assertion attributes you send.
[03:48] Karen (CISO): For audit logs: we need immutable logs, exportable for 7 years, and we want a schema that includes user id, action, resource id, request/response metadata, and IP. What do you retain by default?
[04:02] Priya (SE): Default platform retention is 90 days in the console and audit logs can be exported to your SIEM (S3 or syslog) — retention on our side is configurable for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we can provide longer retention as an add-on; for Private you control retention entirely. We include user id, action, resource, time, request id, model id, route, and where possible request/response size. Note: we redact full prompt content in default logs for privacy but can provide hashed or token-metadata for traceability.
[04:34] Sofia (Cloud Eng): Redaction's important but we need traceability for debugging. Can Redwood provide field-level redaction rules (for PHI) and export raw transcripts to our VPC S3 for processing?
[04:44] Priya (SE): Yes for Private we can ship logs and optionally raw transcripts to your S3 using a VPC endpoint. For Hosted we have a redaction pipeline; raw transcripts are generally not stored unless you opt into longer retention and contract terms due to PHI concern. We recommend Dedicated with BYOK if you want control and export to your own bucket.
[05:05] Dr. Alan (Head of ML): About caching — Alan again — you mentioned KV cache management earlier. If we run on Dedicated or Private can we warm the KV cache across instances? We have batch of few thousand concurrent sessions.
[05:18] Priya (SE): We have continuous batching and shared KV cache strategies in Dedicated; for Private you can choose a topology that pins model instances to scaling groups. The transcript sometimes reads "KV cash" — minor ASR quirk. For very high QPS workloads we recommend Dedicated with pinned pools or Private on the on-prem package to control collocation.
[05:40] Karen (CISO): Data residency — we need all PHI to stay in the EU region for Lacerta's EU patients. Is Redwood able to guarantee region isolation and data residency?
[05:51] Jordan (AE): Yes, we run regional deployment options. Hosted can be region-locked; Dedicated and Private provide stronger guarantees. For strict residency we recommend Private VPC with customer-controlled storage in your region. We'll also include contractual clauses.
[06:06] Sofia (Cloud Eng): What about proof — can we run a security review with our internal GRC? We'll need artifacts: SOC 2 report, pen test summary, architecture diagram, and possibly a runbook for incident response.
[06:18] Jordan (AE): We'll share the SOC 2 Type II, the pen test executive summary (redacted), architecture diagrams, and a 1-pager on incident response.
[06:25] Karen (CISO): Excellent. Also need details on data deletion — if a patient requests deletion do you have an API or process?
[06:31] Priya (SE): Yes we have data deletion APIs and a documented retention lifecycle; for Hosted we can delete records and scrub caches within agreed SLA. For Dedicated/Private you have control over storage so you can enforce deletion in your object stores. We'll provide the retention table mapping actions to timeframes.
[06:48] Dr. Alan (Head of ML): Are there any limitations on model weights or inference artifacts being stored? We sometimes fine-tune models and don't want weights leaving our VPC.
[06:58] Priya (SE): For Private on‑prem you own the model weights entirely; for Dedicated you can either provide weights or use our catalog — if you supply weights they can remain in your VPC if you run Private. For Hosted you can request a model-not-retained contract and we can ensure ephemeral storage. We'll follow up with exact language.
[07:18] Sofia (Cloud Eng): Encryption specifics: which KMS vendors do you support and can you accommodate HSM-backed keys?
[07:25] Priya (SE): We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault for Dedicated/Private. We also support external HSM via KMIP for Private. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption using our KMS; customer BYOK primarily for Dedicated/Private.
[07:40] Karen (CISO): Ok, risk question — if there's a breach in Redwood control plane, how is customer data segmented? How do you notify customers?
[07:49] Jordan (AE): We have segmentation controls and incident response commitments in our SOC 2+ contracts. Notification SLAs vary by severity; high-impact incidents trigger notification within 72 hours and we have a runbook to preserve forensic artifacts. We'll share the IR runbook and typical timeline.
[08:05] Sofia (Cloud Eng): Any known service limitations with Okta SCIM, e.g., group mapping size limits or provisioning latency?
[08:12] Priya (SE): SCIM supports standard group sizes; very large orgs should coordinate with our identity team for bulk provisioning windows. There can be small propagation latency (minutes) depending on Okta polling vs eventing.
[08:26] Alan (Head of ML): What's the typical SLA for latency? We're aiming for sub-200ms P95 on short prompt generations.
[08:34] Priya (SE): Depends on model and sequence length. For the smaller LLMs on Dedicated we regularly see P95 ~80-150ms for short prompts; Hosted varies by region and shared tenancy. Private on colo can achieve lower variance but requires tuned hardware. We'll propose a perf bench with your sample queries to validate.
[08:54] Karen (CISO): Contractually — we need indemnities around PHI handling and clear data processing addendums. Is that standard?
[09:01] Jordan (AE): We have DPAs and can add PHI-specific clauses; indemnity language typically discussed by legal but we can start with standard DPA + BAA conversations if needed.
[09:10] Sofia (Cloud Eng): Quick question — how do you handle audit log immutability? Do you provide append-only stores or write-once buckets?
[09:18] Priya (SE): For Dedicated/Private we can configure WORM on your object storage for immutability and push logs to your SIEM; for Hosted we maintain our own append-only logging with tamper-evident checksums and a signed export capability.
[09:36] Jordan (AE): Ok we're hitting time check — last three items: timeline, pilot scope, and who needs to be involved.
[09:43] Karen (CISO): Timeline: security gating needs to complete by mid-December for product launch window. We'll need artifact delivery this week. Also we want a short pilot in late November.
[09:56] Jordan (AE): Actionable: Jordan to send SOC2 and the ISO gap assessment by 2026-11-24. Priya to draft dedicated vs private comparison with cost and latency (2026-11-29). Sofia to send sample QPS and retention matrix (2026-11-25). We'll aim to stand up a perf bench week of Nov 30.
[10:12] Dr. Alan (Head of ML): Fair. One more minor note — we might run a short canary on Hosted first to compare production traffic shapes vs Dedicated.
[10:19] Priya (SE): We can do that with a controlled routing policy and automatic fallback; good test.
[10:24] Karen (CISO): Anything else from Redwood?
[10:27] Jordan (AE): Nothing else — thanks all. We'll follow up with the artifact pack and set up the perf bench.
[10:33] Speaker 1: (unintelligible)
[10:36] Karen (CISO): Thanks, bye.

Meeting end.
